findings.evidence: dom-1440 lang is "ja" while all body copy is English; screen readers will read the whole page with Japanese pronunciation rules.
findings.after: <html lang="en"> and lang="ja" only on the Japanese inscription span (if kept)
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 3.1.1 Language of Page and 3.1.2 Language of Parts.

findings.where: span.seal '信', span.vertical-inscription, feature numerals 壹 贰 叁
findings.evidence: Decorative glyphs are plain text with no aria-hidden (ariaHidden: null); a screen reader reads '信' and '静寂に進む — Relay 二〇二六' between the hero lede and the trace, and '壹' before 'Intelligent routing'.
findings.after: 信; same for .vertical-inscription and the numerals
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence.

findings.evidence: 'Read the docs' points to #features, not to documentation; nav 'Docs' points to #docs and footer 'Documentation' to '#'. The label promises a destination the link does not reach.
findings.after: Read the docs [DATA NEEDED: docs URL]

findings.evidence: At 375px the red seal '信' sits over the start of the eyebrow, clipping 'AGENT' to 'NT ORCHESTRATION · NOW IN GA' (375-00.png); at 1440 and 1280 the vertical inscription pushes the page 8px wider than the viewport (sweep ROB-003).
findings.before: .seal positioned absolutely over the eyebrow on narrow screens
findings.after: display:none for .seal and .vertical-inscription below 768px, or remove them
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.10 Reflow (content obscured at narrow width).

findings.evidence: Every stop relies on the browser default 'outline: auto 1px'; on the vermilion #c3272b buttons ('Start free', 'Start 14-day trial', 'Get started free') a 1px dark auto ring against red is weak and not guaranteed 3:1 against both the red fill and the cream page.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.7 Focus Visible and 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast.

findings.evidence: 'Start free' appears twice with different targets (hero → #pricing, Starter tier → #); 'Get started' and 'Get started free' both go to '#'.
findings.before: two links named 'Start free' with different destinations
findings.after: Give each the same destination, or distinguish the names ('Start free on Starter')
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose and 3.2.4 Consistent Identification.

findings.evidence: Nav accessible names are 'FEATURES', 'PRICING', 'DOCS' (all-caps in the name, from uppercase source text or text-transform), which some screen readers spell letter by letter.
findings.after: Write 'Features' in the source and apply text-transform in CSS only if caps are kept
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 and 2.5.3 Label in Name (reading of caps).

strengths: Focus order matches the visual order top to bottom with no hidden or covered stops.
Real h1-h3 structure in the body; code sample is real text, not an image.
not_investigated: keyboard operation: no menus, dialogs or custom controls present
